presentation.label: Sample Snap and Crossfade
presentation.summary: Snap native SRC start, end and loop markers to nearby zero crossings. In the normal recording editor, apply an adjustable loop crossfade with one-level undo.
presentation.overview: Snap native SRC start, end and loop markers to nearby zero crossings. In the normal recording editor, apply an adjustable loop crossfade with one-level undo.
highlights: Seek the previous/next zero crossing for start.
Seek a crossing for the actual end, STRT + LEN.
Seek a crossing for the loop return point.
usage: Load a sample on an ONESHOT track and open SRC. Press SRC again if you want the native waveform view.
Release held trigs and TRK. Hold FUNC and turn STRT, LEN or LOOP: left seeks an earlier crossing, right a later crossing. Ordinary turns still work normally.
For a crossfade, make a normal recording and finish it to reach the trim editor. Choose a region, then hold FUNC and turn F to set a short crossfade.
Press FUNC + UP to apply. Audition with the native recorder controls; FUNC + DOWN undoes the edit. Press YES for the normal trim/save workflow.

access.location: ONESHOT/RAM-P1 SRC pages and the native recording trim editor
steps: Load a sample on an ONESHOT track and open SRC. Press SRC again if you want the native waveform view.
Release held trigs and TRK. Hold FUNC and turn STRT, LEN or LOOP: left seeks an earlier crossing, right a later crossing. Ordinary turns still work normally.

controls.name: SRC: FUNC + E — STRT
controls.doc: Seek the previous/next zero crossing for start.

controls.name: SRC: FUNC + F — LEN
controls.doc: Seek a crossing for the actual end, STRT + LEN.

controls.name: SRC: FUNC + G — LOOP
controls.doc: Seek a crossing for the loop return point.

controls.name: Recorder: FUNC + A/C
controls.doc: Seek a crossing for the start/end marker.

controls.name: Recorder: FUNC + F
controls.doc: Set loop crossfade length from 0 to 200 ms.

limitations: SRC snapping works on ONESHOT and RAM-P1. RAM-P1 does not gain a file-backed waveform page.
Exact snapped offsets last for the session; normal quantized parameter values are saved.
No per-step exact snap locks or control-all snap operation. Search is bounded to 4,096 nearby samples.
Crossfades shorten the selected loop by the overlap length. Only the last crossfade can be undone.
Loaded samples and RAM takes have no panel entry into the crossfade editor in 0.2.1. The tutorial uses the normal recorder.
SRC retains its two-page toggle; FUNC + YES remains Save Ptn on SRC.
Conflicts with DIGISLICER, which owns the same SRC key hook.

load.display: Adds 0.8% average, 0.8% worst-case of an audio block over stock (emulator)
load.conditions: Emulator: OS 1.53 on Core 2.1, 8 audio tracks triggering a full-scale sample and 8 MIDI tracks a note on every step at 120 BPM, 3,000 audio blocks timed with the MCF5441x instruction-timing model at 250 MHz, zero-wait memory. Module workload: no Sample Snap and Crossfade action running. Stock: 59.1% average, 61.8% worst block. All six mods together: 73.2% worst block on 1.53, 73.3% on 1.54. Not a hardware measurement.

hardware.summary: sumedho reports the Core 2.1 all-mods builds fully tested and working on a Digitakt 1, OS 1.53 and 1.54, for about one to two hours in total, including project save and reload and a power cycle (2026-10-14): “ok fully tested on hardware and working”.
limitations: Duration is the reporter’s range (1–2 hours) for the combined session across both OS releases; recorded as 90 minutes.
Individual test outcomes were not itemized; standalone (single-mod) hardware coverage is not claimed.
Tested SysEx: 1.53 23503ca42478c1644dea5fd296893f628eafb6662d2ce5e291bfc591f045ae4e, 1.54 257144e4a584172e470c3dde83d7ccda636eeb195b4e5ff0492b3ebc8bdfaba2; firmware was not read back from the device.

tests.summary: Runs on Core 2.1. Emulator regressions on OS 1.53 and 1.54, an emulator CPU-load comparison with stock, and Modwerk source-build parity with the native build are in TESTING.md. sumedho reports this Core 2.1 build fully tested and working on a Digitakt 1, OS 1.53 and 1.54, for about one to two hours including project save/reload and a power cycle (2026-10-14).
